How to choose trail running shoes

Trail running shoes need grip, protection and a secure fit. Lug depth matters on mud. A rock plate protects your feet.

Lug depth and grip

Deeper lugs bite into mud; shallow lugs suit hard-packed trails. Vibram outsoles grip wet rock.

Cushioning and stack height

More cushioning for ultra distances. Heel-to-toe drop changes your stride.

What is a rock plate?

A rock plate is a thin layer that protects against sharp stones.
